close_reason: Verified x509-cert 0.2.5 AlgorithmIdentifier<Any> derives PartialEq with bitwise (Tag, BytesOwned) comparison on Any; the lint behaves as documented. Added three negative-path tests covering all distinguishable mismatch shapes (outer-NULL/inner-absent, outer-absent/inner-NULL, OID-mismatch) plus a DER round-trip oracle confirming decode preserves the Option discriminant. Updated rustdoc to record x509-cert's representation and remove the 'fixture generation out of scope' caveat. Commit fbbd3a33.
description:
pkix-lint/src/rfc5280.rs:516-525 implements the §4.1.1.2 outer-vs-inner signatureAlgorithm match by comparing two AlgorithmIdentifier values with x509-cert's derived PartialEq impl. The rustdoc claims this catches 'NULL parameters on one side, absent parameters on the other' for RFC 4055 §2.1 RSA-PKCS1.

Verification gap: no negative-path fixture exists in the workspace (the rustdoc acknowledges this — 'Fixture generation requires custom DER-level synthesis and is out of scope here'). The lint's positive tests pass on well-formed RSA and ECDSA fixtures, but those tests do not exercise the NULL-vs-absent distinguishing path.

If x509-cert's AlgorithmIdentifier::Parameters is decoded into a normalized form (e.g. both Some(Null) and None decode to the same internal representation) the lint would silently no-op on the exact real-world case it claims to catch. Mozilla SC-068-era CAs produced this mismatch shape.

Hypothesis: derived PartialEq on AlgorithmIdentifier { algorithm: ObjectIdentifier, parameters: Option<Any> } compares parameters field bitwise: Some(Any) != None, and Some(Any { encoded NULL bytes }) != Some(Any { different encoded bytes }). If that holds, the lint behaves as documented.

Probe needed: either (a) read x509-cert/src/ext/* and the Any type's PartialEq impl in der crate, or (b) write a hand-crafted DER cert with mismatched outer/inner identifiers (custom Vec<u8> assembly, not via x509-cert encoder) and feed it through Decode + the lint. If the lint returns Pass on that input, this is a P0 correctness bug. If Error, the lint is correct but the negative test should be added to lock the behavior. Either way the rustdoc claim should be substantiated by an in-tree fixture or external oracle, not a comment.
title: Rfc5280SignatureAlgorithmMatchLint relies on undocumented x509-cert AlgorithmIdentifier PartialEq behavior
